purpose: Canonical claim-to-artifact map. Product plans and work queues are not evidence.

post_alpha_premature_historical.note: Retained for history; do not move or recreate.

claims.summary: Small LM pipelines show held-out exact-copy failures on the synthetic scribe instrument; localization, diversity, scaling/adaptation, pointer, and residual findings remain scoped to their recorded protocols.
Under frozen E1 utility, M1 utility is about 0.999 and official M0 utility about 0.925; the generative LM is not the preferred substrate for this closed task.
claims.limitations: M1 is generator-aligned; runtime/compute reconstruction is partial. The verdict is not a universal claim about language models.

claims.summary: Normalize-then-match rescued 0/486 exact failures. A bounded single-agent rubric pass labeled 0/100 sampled errors faithful.
claims.limitations: This was not independent human or clinician evaluation; inter-rater agreement and broader semantic-equivalence validity remain unmeasured.

claims.summary: Under frozen R-star v1 utility, best classical utility is about 0.638 and generative-plus-verification utility about -1.623, with no sensitivity flip.
claims.limitations: This verdict is specific to R-star v1 and does not establish that generation has no value in other workflows.

claims.summary: On the closed synthetic inst0 fixture, propose-verify-abstain with rules-strong v2 reduced presented error to zero.
claims.limitations: Closed synthetic verifier relation only; this is a regression slice, not an open-world soundness or product-readiness claim.

claims.summary: On sealed synthetic development data, the best of six H2 direct state/pointer checkpoints scored raw 61.82% overall, 64.75% held-value, and 88.40% missing-target accuracy, but 0% absence, 24.80% conflict, 21.60% uncertain, and 1,707 wrong-presented fields. After verification it scored 65.74% overall and zero false-presented fields. H2 failed its frozen raw-plus-final quality gate and was rejected.
limitations: The partition was sealed synthetic development data used for model selection, not an independent test.
Only two seeds and six checkpoints were evaluated.
The post-verification zero false-presented result is verifier behavior and does not repair the failed raw-model gate.
The result rejects this exact H2 architecture and training recipe, not pointer mechanisms or Nano generally.
Latency was intentionally not measured because quality failed, and fresh-v1 remained sealed and unread.
Large checkpoints and row-level evaluation data remain local; no public tag or release anchor currently covers H2.

claims.summary: The training-only-selected H3 evidence-query checkpoint scored raw 56.42% overall, 72.55% held-value, 85.20% missing-target, 45.52% absence, 37.60% conflict, and 38.80% uncertain accuracy on known synthetic development, with zero decode failures and 1,264 wrong-presented fields. It failed frozen uncalibrated admission and was rejected before threshold, verifier, latency, or fresh-v1.
limitations: The partition was known synthetic development data, not an independent test.
Only two seeds and six checkpoints were evaluated.
Perfect training-only calibration versus poor development localizes a transfer problem but does not prove data is its only cause.
The result rejects this exact H3 architecture-plus-training-family intervention, not evidence-query mechanisms or Nano generally.
Threshold, verifier, latency, and fresh-v1 stages were intentionally skipped after uncalibrated admission failed.
Large checkpoints and row-level evaluation data remain local; no public tag or release anchor currently covers H3.

claims.summary: The training-only-selected H4 surface-transfer candidate scored raw 44.96% overall, 38.03% held-value, 53.60% missing-target, 7.99% absence, 22.80% conflict, and 33.60% uncertain accuracy on known synthetic development, with zero decode failures and 2,141 wrong-presented fields. It failed frozen uncalibrated admission and was rejected before threshold, verifier, latency, or fresh-v1.
limitations: The partition was known adaptive synthetic development data, not an independent test or clinical corpus.
Only two seeds and six checkpoints were evaluated.
H4 varied independently partitioned surface/value families while preserving conversation structure, evidence order and distance, distractor policy, architecture, objective, exposure, and gates.
The row-level field and state/span localization is descriptive, not causal.
The result rejects this exact H4 data-only intervention, not broader data work, evidence-query mechanisms, or Nano generally.
Threshold, verifier, latency, and fresh-v1 stages were intentionally skipped after uncalibrated admission failed.
Large checkpoints and row-level evaluation data remain local; no public tag or release anchor currently covers H4.

claims.summary: The training-only-selected H5 fixed 50:50 replay candidate scored raw 78.18% overall, 74.32% held-value, 100% missing-target, 67.80% absence, 59.60% conflict, and 64.80% uncertain accuracy on known synthetic development, with zero decode failures and 1,013 wrong-presented fields. It failed frozen absence, conflict, and uncertainty gates and was rejected before threshold, verifier, latency, or fresh-v1.
limitations: The partition was known adaptive synthetic development data, not an independent test or clinical corpus.
Only two seeds and six checkpoints were evaluated under one frozen 50:50 replay intervention.
H5 rejects this exact mixture, not replay generally, the evidence-query architecture generally, or Nano.
The observed state/span mismatch is descriptive and does not prove that coupling is causal.
Threshold, verifier, latency, and fresh-v1 stages were intentionally skipped after uncalibrated admission failed.
The preregistration records a separate post-freeze historical fresh_v0 metadata review incident outside the H5 evaluator path.
Large checkpoints and row-level evaluation data remain local; no public tag or release anchor currently covers H5.

known_absences: Independent human or clinician E3 validation and inter-rater agreement were not performed.
No current evidence supports clinical deployment or zero-error open-world claims.
